_about: ONE SOURCE ROW THAT HOLDS TWO DECISIONS — split, so one can die while the other lives. Founder, 2026-09-30: 'split DEC - 0002.' A changelog row is written to record a day's work, not to hold one decision, so a single row can carry a structure that is still in force AND a name that was later replaced. Marking the whole row OLD buries the live decision; leaving it IN USE leaves a dead name reading as current. Each split names the source row it comes from, so nothing is invented — the text below is his source row divided, never rewritten.

parts.subject: The four-tab cash-flow surface, and the Budget screen retiring
parts.plain:
Cash flow becomes ONE screen with four tabs, replacing the two separate Cash flow and Budget screens. Four decisions:
1. The Budget screen is RETIRED; its job moves onto the cash-flow surface.
2. Income is entered through a pop-up that asks whether your pay is steady or varies.
3. You can move between past and future months.
4. Big one-off bills get their own list, so a bill that lands once a year is not lost inside a monthly average.
STILL IN FORCE: his approval of the combined cash-flow mock (2026-09-28) carries this architecture forward by name — 'the four-tab architecture from v02'. Only the NAME of the third tab changed; see the row beside this one.

parts.subject: The four tabs were named This month · Income · SPENDING · Debts
parts.plain:
The four tabs were named This month, Income, SPENDING and Debts.
THE THIRD NAME IS DEAD. His synonym ruling of 2026-09-03 — 'money going out in a month → Expenses' — renamed it, and the cash-flow mock he approved on 2026-09-28 shows the tabs as This month · Income · EXPENSES · Debts. The architecture this name sat on is still in force; see the row beside this one.

parts.subject: The average yield of the bonds counts only bonds that have a value today, on that value less accrued interest.
parts.plain: The average yield of the bonds counts only bonds that have a value today, on that value less accrued interest. Before: an unpriced bond added its interest to the top and nothing to the bottom — three bonds read 6.09% where 4.22% is right.

parts.subject: The if-rates-move estimate on a bond is rounded in proportion to the bond’s size, not always to the nearest $1,000.
parts.plain: The if-rates-move estimate on a bond is rounded in proportion to the bond’s size, not always to the nearest $1,000. Before: a $10,000 bond read $10,000 to $10,000 whichever way rates moved.

parts.subject: A sale of shares takes the oldest purchase first.
parts.plain: A sale of shares takes the oldest purchase first. Before: the gain on a sale was worked from an average cost.

parts.subject: A hand-built investment account shows its own uninvested cash inside it.
parts.plain: A hand-built investment account shows its own uninvested cash inside it. Before: the cash it recorded was missing from the account’s own breakdown.

parts.subject: A typed value is called old after six whole months have passed, counted to the day.
parts.plain: A typed value is called old after six whole months have passed, counted to the day. Before: it counted month names crossed, so 30 April read six months old on 1 October.

parts.subject: Any account that already lists holdings can take a recorded buy or sale.
parts.plain: Any account that already lists holdings can take a recorded buy or sale. Before: a fixed-income brokerage holding bond funds could not be chosen.

parts.subject: A Roth 401(k) is its own choice when adding an account: a 401(k) in the Roth tax bucket.
parts.plain: A Roth 401(k) is its own choice when adding an account: a 401(k) in the Roth tax bucket. Before: the form had no Roth 401(k).

parts.subject: A maturity date makes an account Bonds & CDs before its name is read; property that is not a house is personal property.
parts.plain: A maturity date makes an account Bonds & CDs before its name is read; property that is not a house is personal property. Before: a CD named ‘savings’ read as cash, and a ring could be filed as real estate.

parts.subject: A 529 is tax-free for education and an HSA is pre-tax but tax-free for medical costs, and their pages say so.
parts.plain: A 529 is tax-free for education and an HSA is pre-tax but tax-free for medical costs, and their pages say so. Before: a 529 read ‘taxable’ and an HSA read ‘taxed when it comes out’.

parts.subject: Cash a hand-built account records for itself is on the Cash line; a holding with no price is never counted as cash.
parts.plain: Cash a hand-built account records for itself is on the Cash line; a holding with no price is never counted as cash. Before: that cash was in no Cash line, and an unpriced holding’s value could fall into cash.

parts.subject: Investments is one function, and Cash + Investments always equals Cash and investments together.
parts.plain: Investments is one function, and Cash + Investments always equals Cash and investments together. Before: the Investments line was added up in more than one place.

parts.subject: No two accounts show the same name: alike names are numbered · 1, · 2 in the order the accounts were made.
parts.plain: No two accounts show the same name: alike names are numbered · 1, · 2 in the order the accounts were made. Before: two accounts could read the same.

parts.subject: A holding nobody has classed is Unclassified everywhere, and the words under an account count holdings by that same test.
parts.plain: A holding nobody has classed is Unclassified everywhere, and the words under an account count holdings by that same test. Before: Net worth said Unclassified and the account page said Stocks / Funds.

parts.subject: The return on the retirement money weighs each account by the money set aside for retirement.
parts.plain: The return on the retirement money weighs each account by the money set aside for retirement. Kept as built; the reviewer wanted a different weighting (held).

parts.subject: Home’s investments figure is Performance’s ending value, read from the accounts.
parts.plain: Home’s investments figure is Performance’s ending value, read from the accounts. Before: Home showed Net worth’s Investments line, lower by a linked account’s uninvested cash.

parts.subject: A money-market fund a broker flags is kept as a holding, not dropped.
parts.plain: A money-market fund a broker flags is kept as a holding, not dropped. Before: such funds vanished at sync.

parts.subject: The person’s own answer about a holding’s class outranks what its name suggests.
parts.plain: The person’s own answer about a holding’s class outranks what its name suggests. Before: the name won.

parts.subject: Only a vehicle can be the car you drive.
parts.plain: Only a vehicle can be the car you drive. Before: a jewellery collection worth more than the car was taken as the car.

parts.subject: The rate the retirement money grows at, and its spread, are blended over exactly the money set aside, with no figure when nothing is set aside.
parts.plain: The rate the retirement money grows at, and its spread, are blended over exactly the money set aside, with no figure when nothing is set aside. Before: an invented 6% and 12% stood in.

parts.subject: With nothing owned there is no average return.
parts.plain: With nothing owned there is no average return. Before: it said 7%.

parts.plain: Monthly contributions: the 401(k) answer is held at the yearly legal limit for the age reached this year; property savings do not count; nothing answered gives no figure. Before: no limit, property savings counted, and $0 for nothing answered.

parts.subject: History shared is counted in months and never rounded up to a year.
parts.plain: History shared is counted in months and never rounded up to a year. Before: eighteen months read ‘2 years’.

parts.subject: Itemising never lowers an account’s total; whatever is not itemised stays as cash.
parts.plain: Itemising never lowers an account’s total; whatever is not itemised stays as cash. Before: a part-itemised $186,442 could fall to $148,001.

parts.subject: Accounts made by itemising carry the original’s retirement share, source and wrapper; a bond’s face value is entered or left blank.
parts.plain: Accounts made by itemising carry the original’s retirement share, source and wrapper; a bond’s face value is entered or left blank. Before: itemising moved money out of the nest egg and gave bonds an invented face value.

parts.plain: The list under the class rows uses the same split as the rows, and one institution typed two ways is one group. Before: its Cash group read $8,000 while the Cash row read $8,838.

parts.plain: With nothing held there is no growth figure for alternatives. Before: it showed $0 growth.

parts.subject: A money-market settlement fund is a fund, and a bond word inside a company name is not a bond.
parts.plain: A money-market settlement fund is a fund, and a bond word inside a company name is not a bond. Before: a settlement fund read as cash; Treasury Wine Estates read as a bond.

parts.subject: With two or more properties and no use stated, the one entered first is the home; the others count toward retirement.
parts.plain: With two or more properties and no use stated, the one entered first is the home; the others count toward retirement. Before: every such property was the home, so a second property fell out of the retirement money.

parts.plain: A bond’s face value or rate that was never entered stays blank — never $0 — and the screens say ‘not entered’. Before: a CD typed by its balance showed a yield to maturity of −274%.

parts.plain: A year’s interest from a bond or CD has one rule everywhere: face × rate; with no face, value × rate; with no rate, $0 and said so. Before: the Bonds screen counted a CD at $0 while the income figure counted balance × rate.

parts.subject: A bond or CD past its maturity date pays no more interest.
parts.plain: A bond or CD past its maturity date pays no more interest. Before: it kept counting a year’s coupon.

parts.subject: Yield to maturity uses the value less accrued interest, like the current yield.
parts.plain: Yield to maturity uses the value less accrued interest, like the current yield. Before: it used the value with accrued interest and read too low (3.76% where 4.57% is right).

parts.subject: The if-rates-move estimate measures the change between two prices worked the same way, and a CD gets no estimate.
parts.plain: The if-rates-move estimate measures the change between two prices worked the same way, and a CD gets no estimate. Before: a 4.4-year Treasury read down about $1,000 where about $1,700 is right; only the screen hid a CD’s figure.

parts.subject: Years to maturity count calendar days, not the time of day.
parts.plain: Years to maturity count calendar days, not the time of day. Before: the hour shaved part of a day off (one example moved from 5.66% to 5.65%).

parts.subject: The sweep that corrects classes never changes an account the person confirmed.
parts.plain: The sweep that corrects classes never changes an account the person confirmed. Before: it could overwrite a confirmed class.

parts.plain: A saved record whose accounts were all deleted shows the first-day screen, not $0 owned. Before: it showed $0 with a 7% average return.

parts.plain: The retirement money’s twelve-month return weighs each account by what was set aside when the year began: Σ now ÷ Σ start − 1. Before: weighed by today’s amounts, 13.72% where 12.98% is right.

parts.subject: A 529’s and an HSA’s tax words are fixed by what they are; ‘(Roth)’ appears only for an account in the Roth bucket.
parts.plain: A 529’s and an HSA’s tax words are fixed by what they are; ‘(Roth)’ appears only for an account in the Roth bucket. Before: a 529 stated tax-free read ‘tax-free (Roth)’.

parts.subject: A hand-built account is split holding by holding, so a T-bill inside it is Bonds & CDs.
parts.plain: A hand-built account is split holding by holding, so a T-bill inside it is Bonds & CDs. Before: everything but its cash was filed under the account’s own class.

parts.subject: A Roth 401(k) reads Roth 401(k), and a tax-advantaged account with no kind and known digits shows its tax word.
parts.plain: A Roth 401(k) reads Roth 401(k), and a tax-advantaged account with no kind and known digits shows its tax word. Before: ‘Fidelity 401(k)’ for both a Roth and a pre-tax 401(k); ‘Vanguard -1234’ for a Roth.

parts.subject: A holding with nothing stored — no tag, no kind, nothing in its name — is Unclassified, never Stocks / Funds by default.
parts.plain: A holding with nothing stored — no tag, no kind, nothing in its name — is Unclassified, never Stocks / Funds by default. Before: it was filed as Stocks / Funds (against DEC-2160).

parts.plain: Broker Treasury wording (TREAS, UST, T-bond) counts as a Treasury in the words under an account, and more than one reads Treasuries. Before: a broker’s T-bill read ‘1 bond’.

parts.subject: A value dated by its month alone is shown as the 1st of that month.
parts.plain: A value dated by its month alone is shown as the 1st of that month. Before: the stored text was handed back unchanged.

parts.subject: Performance draws no walk for a window its record exists but cannot reach; a sentence names the record’s first day.
parts.plain: Performance draws no walk for a window its record exists but cannot reach; a sentence names the record’s first day. Before: the beginning was worked back from today and wealth generated shown as if measured.

parts.subject: A rate the person set themselves is labelled an estimate.
parts.plain: A rate the person set themselves is labelled an estimate. Before: it took the record’s flag.

parts.subject: An employer’s percent match is taken on the 401(k) figure after the yearly limit.
parts.plain: An employer’s percent match is taken on the 401(k) figure after the yearly limit. Before: on the figure as typed — $1,600 where $1,490 is right.

parts.subject: History shared is rounded down and its sentence built from whole months only.
parts.plain: History shared is rounded down and its sentence built from whole months only. Before: one day short of a year read ‘1 year’.

parts.subject: Accounts made by itemising carry the typical rate for their class, never 0%, and a bond rate not entered stays blank.
parts.plain: Accounts made by itemising carry the typical rate for their class, never 0%, and a bond rate not entered stays blank. Before: every itemised account had a 0% rate.

parts.plain: The Other investments summary reads the class split, so its total is the Alternatives line’s dollars and each part is rated by what it is. Before: whole accounts only — $18,641 where the Alternatives line read $23,031.

parts.subject: A property’s name is not read as evidence of its class; a fund that writes options is a fund.
parts.plain: A property’s name is not read as evidence of its class; a fund that writes options is a fund. Before: ‘Silver Lake house’ read as an alternative and a covered-call ETF as options.

parts.subject: What a property is for has one reading for every function; handed the rent entries, a property is a rental only when an entry names it, and a household with no home is told so.
parts.plain: What a property is for has one reading for every function; handed the rent entries, a property is a rental only when an entry names it, and a household with no home is told so. Before: three functions read it three ways; a rented-out house marked home counted as the home.

parts.subject: Years to maturity are exact, by anniversaries: one year to the day is exactly 1.
parts.plain: Years to maturity are exact, by anniversaries: one year to the day is exactly 1. Before: days ÷ 365.25 (0.9993 for one year).

parts.plain: A bond is priced at exact times, its yearly coupon on each maturity anniversary; a matured bond or one with no date has no price. Before: years rounded to a whole number, at least 1, so a matured bond still paid.

parts.plain: The accrued-interest note shows only for a bond that pays interest and has no accrued figure entered. Before: a zero-coupon bond got the note.
